 Detailed Forecast
 Synopsis
 Another high pressure system just north of the Hawaiian Islands will drift southeast and weaken through Thursday. A stronger high builds in north of the state by Friday, briefly increasing trade wind speeds. Two passing upper level disturbances will keep wet trade wind weather in the forecast through the end of this week. The subtropical ridge will settle in over the island chain by early next week with an extended drying trend in the forecast.
 Discussion
 The satellite imagery this morning shows cloud bands northeast of the Hawaiian Islands are appearing more stable and showing signs of a lowering of the trade wind temperature inversion heights. Upper air balloon soundings taken at 2 AM HST (12Z) from Lihue and Hilo are observing the temperature inversion height around 5,000 and 8,000 feet respectively. These upper air soundings validate the differences in stability between the clouds near Kauai and clouds near the Big Island of Hawaii.
The wet trade wind weather pattern will continue across the state for the next few days as two passing upper level disturbances will produce enough lift for continued periods of shower activity lasting into the weekend. These showers and light to moderate rainfall amounts will tend to favor windward mountain areas of all islands. Some of the stronger shower bands will bring brief rainfall to leeward areas during this time period.
A small break in the shower trends may develop this afternoon, then enhanced shower activity picks up again as the diurnal rainfall pattern returns this evening. Another upper level trough moves across the region from Friday into Saturday, once again enhancing shower activity as increasing trade winds lift unsettled clouds up and over the windward mountain slopes of each island.
A complete change in the weather pattern will begin early next week, as the larger scale subtropical ridge settles in over the Hawaii region. Large scale downward vertical motions, or subsidence, will stabilize the atmosphere by lowering the temperature inversion heights through increasing subsidence (drying and warming the air). Expect a change to drier trade wind weather from Monday through Wednesday as global model cross sections show temperature inversion heights falling into the 4,000 to 5,000 foot range significantly limiting vertical cloud development. Expect cooler feeling air as relative humidity levels drop through at least next week Wednesday.
 Aviation
 Moderate to locally breezy trade winds are expected through today, before gradually strengthening Thursday through Friday. Showers will primarily impact windward and mountain areas, with possible spillover into leeward areas. These showers will be more frequent overnight. Expect MVFR conditions within most showers, while VFR prevails elsewhere.
AIRMET Sierra is in effect for windward areas of Oahu, Molokai, Maui, and the Big Island. Conditions over windward areas of the smaller islands are expected to gradually improve by morning, while windward Big Island may still see mountain obscurations until this afternoon. Mountain obscurations will be more likely tonight due to overnight showers.
AIRMET Tango remains in effect below 7000 feet for low level moderate turbulence over and downwind of island terrain. These conditions are expected to be borderline through today, but will be more prevalent when the winds strengthen Thursday through Friday. Light to moderate turbulence aloft, particularly between FL300 and FL360, is also possible today due to an upper level low moving across the state. Expect conditions to last from morning through late afternoon.
 Marine
 Trade winds will hover in the fresh to locally strong range through Thursday. A Small Craft Advisory (SCA) remains in effect for the typically windy waters around Big Island and Maui County through Thursday as a series of highs and fronts quickly pass well north of Hawaii. Trades will strengthen again Thursday night and Friday as a stronger high passes north of the state, likely necessitating an expansion of the SCA in area. Trades may begin to weaken slightly by this weekend.
A small, medium-period north (010 degrees) swell will continue to decline today. Surf along north and west-facing shores will decline somewhat this morning, then hold steady with the arrival of a new small, north- northwest swell that peaks this afternoon and evening. Surf will continue to decline on Thursday as the new swell fades. Another small north-northwest swell is forecast to arrive and build on Saturday, peaking Saturday night into Sunday, with a larger swell possible next Tuesday.
Rough surf along east-facing shores will hold near seasonal averages today into Thursday. A slight increase in east shore surf is expected Friday and Saturday as trade winds strengthen. Mainly small background level surf is expected along south-facing shores during the next several days. A small bump is possible this afternoon for south-facing shores with a medium-period swell. Another small, long- period swell brings a bump to south shore surf on Friday.
 Fire weather
 Wet trade wind weather will continue into the weekend with periods of showers favoring windward mountain areas. Trade winds will increase a bit on Friday as high pressure builds in north of the islands. However, humidity levels will remain elevated enough to limit critical fire behavior concerns. Even increasing wind speeds over higher elevation areas on Friday will see higher minimum humidity levels lasting through the weekend. An extended period of drier trade wind weather returns for much of next week. Temperature inversion heights near Maui and the Big Island today will range from 6,500 to 7,500 feet elevation.
 HFO Watches/Warnings/Advisories
 Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST Thursday for Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel, Alenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters, Big Island Southeast Waters.
